about.title: El Cajon Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: El Cajon sits where I-8 threads through the east county, and a lot of the city's traffic funnels onto that freeway or along Broadway, E Main Street, and Fletcher Parkway. Those four corridors show up most often in public collision records for the city. In 2025, El Cajon logged 619 injury collisions, with 891 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to be when reported crashes cluster, which lines up with the end-of-week commute. If one of those numbers now includes you, the weeks ahead can feel like a second job. Adjusters call. Bills arrive before the pain settles. LawProactive exists to take one task off that list: we connect you, at no cost, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles San Diego County car accident claims. We are not a law firm. The attorney you speak with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers money. You keep control; we simply make the introduction.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cajon Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock in California is real
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but if a government vehicle or public agency is involved, the deadline can shrink to six months. Getting connected early keeps those options open.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some blame; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: Free to connect, contingency to hire
items.desc: LawProactive charges you nothing, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in ordinary car crash cases.

items.question: I was hit on I-8 near El Cajon but the other driver's insurer keeps calling. Do I have to give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and doing so early can be used to minimize your claim. It is reasonable to politely decline and let an attorney handle those conversations. Focus instead on saving photos, the CHP or El Cajon Police report number, and any witness contacts.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in El Cajon?
items.answer: Under California law you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a city bus, county vehicle, or other public entity was involved, you may need to file a government claim within six months. Because that shorter window comes up more than people expect, it helps to talk with an attorney soon after the crash.

items.question: The insurer says I was partly at fault. Does that end my case?
items.answer: Not in California. The state uses pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you, but you are not barred from recovering. Evidence like dashcam footage, skid marks, and intersection camera records along Broadway or Fletcher Parkway can matter a great deal in that fault discussion, so preserve what you can.
